summary: Cascading Style Sheets: layout engines, the box model, responsive typography, and visual animation systems.

rows.means: includes padding and border inside total width and height
rows.consequence: The universal CSS reset invariant. With content-box, adding 10px padding makes a 100px element 120px wide, causing layout overflow.

rows.means: tag selector / class selector / unique identifier selector
rows.consequence: An identifier selector carries high specificity and is correspondingly hard to override later; a class selector is weaker and composes, which is why maintainable sheets are built from classes.

rows.means: space outside the border / space inside the border
rows.consequence: Margins separate sibling elements and collapse vertically. Padding adds breathing room between the border and the element's inner content.

rows.means: activates one-dimensional flexible box layout engine
rows.consequence: Lays out direct children along a single main axis (row or column) with automated space distribution and alignment.

rows.means: sets the primary axis direction of flex items
rows.consequence: row (default) arranges items horizontally left-to-right; column arranges items vertically top-to-bottom.

rows.means: alignment along the main axis / alignment along the cross axis
rows.consequence: justify-content (flex-start, center, space-between) aligns along the flow direction; align-items aligns perpendicular to it.

rows.means: space between flex or grid items
rows.consequence: Replaces messy margin hacks on children. Automatically handles spacing without unwanted outer margins on first or last items.

rows.means: controls how a flex item expands or contracts
rows.consequence: flex-grow allows the item to fill leftover space; flex-shrink allows it to contract under overflow; flex-basis sets initial size.

rows.means: activates two-dimensional grid layout engine
rows.consequence: Simultaneously coordinates rows and columns with explicit track definitions and gap spacing.

rows.means: responsive auto-wrapping grid with no media queries
rows.consequence: Creates as many 280px+ columns as will fit into the container width, expanding them equally to fill remaining space.

rows.code: position: static | relative | absolute | fixed | sticky
rows.means: determines how an element is positioned in the viewport or parent
rows.consequence: relative keeps space in flow; absolute removes from flow relative to closest positioned ancestor; fixed pins to viewport; sticky sticks on scroll.

rows.code: top / right / bottom / left and z-index
rows.means: offset distances from anchor / stacking order along the Z-axis
rows.consequence: z-index only takes effect on positioned elements (relative, absolute, fixed, sticky) or flex/grid children.

rows.means: explicit size, fluid ceiling limit, and minimum floor size
rows.consequence: max-width: 100% prevents images, tables, and containers from breaking out of parent boundaries on mobile screens.

rows.code: rem vs em vs vh / vw vs %
rows.means: font-relative and viewport-relative length units
rows.consequence: rem is relative to the root font size, so it respects a reader who has changed it; em is relative to the parent, so it compounds when nested; the viewport units are a hundredth of the viewport's width or height.

rows.means: text foreground color / container background surface color
rows.consequence: Text needs a contrast ratio of at least 4.5 to 1 against its background to meet the accessibility guidelines at level AA, with large text allowed 3 to 1. The ratios are thresholds rather than targets to round towards, and the reason for them is readers with moderately low vision who are not using any assistive technology.

rows.means: prioritized font fallback stack
rows.consequence: The browser attempts to render the first font; if not installed or loaded, falls back down the list to system defaults.

rows.means: vertical distance between text baselines
rows.consequence: Using unitless numbers (e.g. 1.5) scales proportionally with any font-size, preventing clipped descenders and cramped paragraphs.

rows.means: behavior when content exceeds its container bounds
rows.consequence: auto adds scrollbars only when content overflows; hidden clips overflow cleanly; visible (default) spills outside container bounds.

rows.code: opacity vs visibility: hidden vs display: none
rows.means: visual transparency / invisible but in layout / completely removed from layout
rows.consequence: display: none removes element from layout and accessibility tree; visibility: hidden keeps layout space; opacity changes transparency.

rows.means: smoothly animates property changes between states
rows.consequence: Animate transform and opacity for smooth 60fps GPU acceleration; avoid animating width, height, or top which trigger CPU layout reflows.

rows.means: GPU-accelerated geometric transformations
rows.consequence: Transforms do not trigger layout or repaint, which is why they are the ones to reach for when animating something the reader is watching.

rows.means: defines multi-step CSS keyframe animation sequence
rows.consequence: Paired with animation: spin 1s linear infinite to create continuous or complex visual transitions.

rows.means: interactive user state pseudo-classes
rows.consequence: :focus-visible displays keyboard focus rings only for keyboard navigators, keeping mouse clicks clean while preserving accessibility.

rows.means: targets elements by their numeric position among siblings
rows.consequence: Used for zebra striping tables, alternating grid cards, or styling specific rows without extra HTML classes.

rows.means: pseudo-elements that insert decorative content into CSS
rows.consequence: Requires the content property to exist at all. Used for icons, tooltips and accent lines without adding elements to the document that mean nothing.

rows.means: CSS custom properties (design tokens and variables)
rows.consequence: Unlike a preprocessor's variables, which are substituted before the sheet ships, these are live: they cascade, can be changed at run time, and are read by the element that uses them — which is what makes a theme switch a change to one value.

rows.means: performs mathematical calculations across mixed units
rows.consequence: Allows subtracting absolute lengths (e.g. 2rem) from fluid percentages (100%), solving complex responsive layouts.

rows.means: bounds a value between an absolute floor and ceiling
rows.consequence: clamp(1rem, 2.5vw, 2.5rem) creates fluid responsive typography that scales with the screen without ever getting too small or huge.

rows.means: mobile-first responsive viewport breakpoint query
rows.consequence: Applies styling rules only when the screen is at least 768px wide, allowing clean progression from mobile to tablet to desktop.

rows.means: component-level container queries
rows.consequence: Applies styles based on the width of the parent container rather than the entire browser window, enabling truly modular components.

rows.means: controls how or
rows.consequence: cover fills the container while preserving aspect ratio (cropping excess); contain scales without cropping (leaving letterboxes).

rows.means: sets the mouse cursor icon for user feedback
rows.consequence: Provides clear tactile affordance that an element can be clicked, dragged, or is currently disabled.
